caption: Average Change in INC score from combined layer to base layer, where a negative score means the base layer was better than the combined one and vice versa. The gray and orange bars indicate whether the input to the compression layer is inferred frames or lexical signal, respectively. In all cases, inferred frames has a better effect on base layer and lexical signal has improved combined layer's performance.
model_annotation: This chart illustrates the average change in INC score from a combined layer to a base layer, differentiating between inputs of inferred frames and lexical signals. The horizontal axis represents observation probability, labeled with values of 0.2, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7, and 0.9, with equally spaced intervals. The vertical axis is labeled “Average Change Using Compression,” with a linear scale ranging from -3 to 2, and tick labels at intervals of 1. Two sets of bars are present, differentiated by color: gray bars representing inferred frames and tan bars representing lexical signal inputs. The inferred frames bars are consistently shorter than the lexical signal bars, ranging in approximate height from -2.5 to -0.4. Conversely, the lexical signal bars have approximate heights ranging from 0.2 to 2, with the tallest bar at 0.9 having a height of approximately 2. A legend is provided near the bottom right corner of the chart, identifying the gray and tan bars as representing inferred frames and lexical signal, respectively. The bars are sorted in ascending order of observation probability along the horizontal axis, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond the use of color to differentiate the data sets.
